symbols.limits: reads/writes: the component views in the parameters of the system's exported methods. uses: the component operations (add, remove, get, has) its per-frame update performs through the engine's out-of-line helpers, itself or in a function it calls (depth 2), with the call site; kind index: a matched method reads the type's index and the operation is not known. Not listed: operations the compiler inlined, those deeper than depth 2, and what a method that is not the update does (e.g. a SystemLoad) - read its pseudo-code; an empty writes list is not "writes nothing".

does.text: Takes one finished hit (an action originator plus a hit description with its damage) and, once a validity check on the target passes, creates a new entity carrying esv::hit::HitResultEventOneFrameComponent (0x1f0 bytes) holding the originator, the hit description, and a few flags derived from the hit; the event lives one frame. A second creation of the same event happens on another path of the same function (an early branch that handles a different target kind), with its flag byte forced to 0.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll (Toolkit build) pseudo-code, HitSystem::ProcessHit at +0x3CA500 (413 lines, CreateEntity at lines 300 and 396, searched and read in windows). The add helper FUN_1803c0550 -> FUN_1803c0c20 (+0x3C0C20) ends in AllocRaw 0x1f0 with _DAT_182202bcc -> init +0x552A0 -> 'esv::hit::HitResultEventOneFrameComponent'. One text in the function says items cannot dodge attacks, which is a design note in the code, not a behaviour I traced

does.text: For each queued hit request it walks the damage entries of the hit description. On paths whose conditions were read only partly (damage entries; a spell-prototype flag bit when there are none) it creates a new entity carrying esv::hit::HitNotificationRequestOneFrameComponent (0x48 bytes), which feeds HitNotificationSystem. On the hit's entity it adds the hit data components eoc::hit::TargetComponent (0xb8 bytes), eoc::hit::AttackerComponent, eoc::hit::WeaponComponent and eoc::hit::ThrownObjectComponent, copied from the request; which branch adds which (for instance whether ThrownObject needs a thrown object in the hit) was not read, so the conditions are unknown.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll (Toolkit build) pseudo-code, HitSystem::ProcessHitRequests at +0x3CB050 (624 lines). Adds: FUN_1803c0490 -> FUN_1803c0a00 (+0x3C0A00, 0x48, DAT_182202438 -> +0x53D40 'esv::hit::HitNotificationRequestOneFrameComponent'); FUN_1803c1750 (0xb8, DAT_1821fee58 -> 'eoc::hit::TargetComponent'); FUN_1803c0600 (8 bytes, DAT_1821fee50 -> 'eoc::hit::AttackerComponent'); FUN_1803c1c40 (8, DAT_1821fee54 -> 'eoc::hit::WeaponComponent'); FUN_1803c1a40 (8, DAT_182202b84 -> 'eoc::hit::ThrownObjectComponent'); all end in AllocRaw (adds). The trigger for each add (which branch) was read only partly

does.text: Destroys, with the deferred buffer, every entity matched by two queries (the one-frame hit event entities, by the pattern), so they last one frame.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll (Toolkit build) pseudo-code, HitSystem::CleanupOneFrameComponents at +0x3C89E0: two DestroyEntity loops. The queries' contents were not resolved, so the claim that they hold the one-frame entities is an inference from the method name and the pattern
